# CANDIDATE: OPENING_RANGE_CLOSE_LOCATION_BREAKOUT

**Filed:** 2026-07-09  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

The average closing position within the first 6 five-minute opening range candles (9:35-10:05 ET) captures intraday bias that predicts breakout direction when price breaches the opening range boundaries (9:30-10:00 ET) with expanding volume. This edge exists because persistent closing bias near one boundary of the opening range indicates institutional accumulation/distribution, increasing the probability of a directional break when volume confirms the move.

## Mechanism

**Entry:**  
- Calculate average close location for candles 9:35-10:05 ET: `avg = sum((close - low)/(high - low)) for each of 6 candles / 6`  
- If `avg > 0.6` AND price closes above ORB high (9:30-10:00) on a candle with volume > 1.5x average ORB candle volume → long  
- If `avg < 0.4` AND price closes below ORB low on a candle with volume > 1.5x average ORB volume → short  

**Exit:**  
- Initial stop: opposite ORB boundary (below ORB low for long, above ORB high for short)  
- Primary target: 2x ORB width from entry  
- Alternative management: trail stop at 15% chandelier below new highs (long) or above new lows (short) after entry  
- Time filter: only consider entries between 9:30-11:00 ET; avoid low volume days (VIX < 12 proxy)

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+ account; $1K paper account equals ~14% headline P&L scaling (based on 50% risk-per-trade cap and $1.00 avg entry premium).  
2. **Sample bias:** Proposed logic uses only price/volume from 9:30-10:05 ET window; sample size would be all trading days in backtest period; overfit risk exists due to parameter thresholds (0.6/0.4 close location, 1.5x volume) requiring walk-forward validation.  
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (no walk-forward held-out window performed yet).  
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (no validation of simulated vs actual OPRA fills on top 3 J days).  
5. **Failure modes:**  
   - Worst day: false breakout with low volume triggering stop at opposite ORB boundary  
   - Max drawdown: consecutive losing days during low-volume/choppy markets (VIX < 12)  
   - Blow-up scenario: volatility expansion causing ORB to widen dramatically, increasing stop distance beyond premium capacity  
6. **Concentration:** unknown -- requires Stage-1 backtest to determine if top-5 days exceed 20% of P&L (would disclose if >50%).
